name: Hamba NW of Nachingwea south of Mbemkuru River

earlier_scan.note: Extinct, unclassifiable Tanzanian variety; Glottolog lists zero references.

sources.citation: Glottolog languoid record hamb1239 (hid NOCODE_Hamba; family Unclassifiable; AES extinct; Glottolog's most extensive description list = Batibo 1992, Crosse-Upcott 1956; zero descriptive refs).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)

sources.citation: Crosse-Upcott, A.R.W. 1956. The social structure of the KiNgindo-speaking peoples. PhD thesis, University of Cape Town (709-page OpenUCT scan with scanned layer; incl. Part 'Internal variations of Ngindoland', pp. 348-360 = Glottolog hh:608174, the item Glottolog ties to hamb1239 'Proto-Hamba').
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on Hamba speech at all: p. 354 (PDF p. 417, verified on page image) 'There is no knowing whether or not the aboriginal Hamba or Ikemba spoke kiNgindo.. Present Hamba and Ikemba speech is scarcely distinguishable from kiMagingo.' No Hamba wordlist or linguistic data anywhere (Appendix B 'Neo-Hamba' column = kiNdonde speakers of Kilimarondo, a different group). The thesis's only accent remark (p. 26, PDF p. 30: Ngindo 'accentuating the first syllable of the stem, as opposed to the penultimate') is about kiNgindo (ngin1244), not an anterior Hamba language.
Page concerns only the Congolese Hamba (Tetela cluster, ISO hba); nothing on the Tanzanian Hamba.

sources.citation: Batibo, Herman. 1992. The fate of ethnic languages in Tanzania. In M. Brenzinger (ed.), Language Death: Factual and Theoretical Explorations with Special Reference to East Africa, 85-98. Berlin: Mouton de Gruyter.
